patch.value: The SDK surface gate classifies every signature text change as breaking, so an optional field added to a host-built context needs the same acknowledgement as a removed export

Found while landing pm-wb6ktl (2026-11-16). scripts/sdk-surface-snapshot.mjs compares each exported symbol's printed signature text, and any difference is reported as breaking. Adding an optional, host-set field to BeforeMutationHookContext (a context the host constructs and hands to guards, so no implementer is affected) and widening runRegisteredMutationGuardForTest from Promise<void> to Promise<MutationGuardOverride[] | undefined> were both reported as breaking, so an additive SDK change needs the same recorded acknowledgement as a removed export. The gate's own acceptance criteria (pm-e6tm5c) classify changes as additive, compatible or breaking, but no signature change is ever classed as compatible. The cost: breaking_acknowledgements fills with false positives, which hides the real breaks reviewers and release notes must see. Proposal: classify signature changes by position. A new optional property on an object type is compatible. A new required property on a type the caller supplies, or any removed property, is breaking. A return type widened from void, and a parameter made optional, are compatible. Keep a removed export and a narrowed input as breaking. Record the classification reason with each change. Duplicate check: searched sdk surface snapshot breaking signature optional property additive. pm-e6tm5c (closed) delivered the gate; no open item covers classification precision.

An optional property added to an exported object type is classified compatible, not breaking; A removed export, a removed property or a new required property on a caller-supplied type stays breaking; Each classified change records the reason the classifier used, and the spec covers one example of each class
Only caller-visible incompatibilities require a breaking acknowledgement
Any signature text difference, including an added optional field, is reported as breaking
